description: Historical listicle videos — numbered lists of people, events, or facts from history

mgPreferences.when: listicle item transition (Number 9, Number 1, etc.) — announce each new item
the item number itself (#9, #1) or a single shocking word from the narration
first time a person is introduced with their name and title/role
sequence of dates or years mentioned (1915, 1925, 1999)
direct quotes spoken verbatim in the narration
citing books, memoirs, interviews, or official statements
specific numbers (5 million members, 32000 mourners, 3 Academy Awards)
a specific city or location is central to the scene
explicit contrast between two things (public vs private, image vs reality)
rare — only for the single most pivotal quote or revelation in the entire video

footageRules: When a PERSON is named → web-image (their real photo)
When a filmed EVENT is described (speech, protest, ceremony) → youtube
When a BOOK, DOCUMENT, or NEWSPAPER is mentioned → web-image
When NO specific entity — just mood/atmosphere → stock
Item introduction scenes (Number 9, etc.) → web-image of that person's face
Transition scenes between items → stock B-roll for visual breathing room

pacing.sceneDuration: 6-10 seconds per scene, slightly longer for emotional moments
pacing.textAppearance: fade-slide for lowerThirds, wipe for headlines at item transitions

sceneStructure.footage: Most dramatic or shocking image from the story — the person or event that hooks viewers
sceneStructure.notes: Open with the main subject. If it's about a person naming others, show THAT person first. Tease the most shocking item.

sceneStructure.footage: Historical context — archival photos, era-establishing shots, the main subject in their prime
sceneStructure.notes: Set the stage. Who is this person? Why does their list matter? Build credibility before the countdown.

sceneStructure.footage: Each numbered item: ALWAYS show the person's photo first, then supporting footage (their work, events, locations)
sceneStructure.notes: Pattern per item: 1) headline/focusWord with item number, 2) person's photo with lowerThird, 3) supporting scenes with evidence. More scenes for higher-ranked items.

sceneStructure.footage: Return to the main subject, reflective imagery, the lasting impact
sceneStructure.notes: Wrap up the emotional arc. What does this list mean? Why does it matter today?
Subscribe prompt — keep it short, let the story's weight carry the CTA

keywordRules.itemIntroduction: When a numbered item is introduced (e.g. 'Number 9, DW Griffith'), the keyword MUST be that person's name — not a generic description
keywordRules.entityFirst: If a scene mentions a real person by name, keyword = their name. Always. No exceptions.
keywordRules.supportingScenes: Scenes within an item's section that don't mention the person by name can use contextual keywords (their movies, events, locations)
keywordRules.noScreenplayKeywords: Keywords are search terms, NOT cinematic shot descriptions. 'DW Griffith' not 'stern man in bow tie at film studio'

mgRules.itemTransition: Every numbered item transition MUST get a headline or focusWord MG — this is the visual cue that we're moving to the next item
mgRules.personIntro: First mention of each person in the list gets a lowerThird with their name and brief title
mgRules.noCluster: Never put MGs on more than 2 consecutive scenes — leave breathing room
mgRules.quotesOnly: callout and articleHighlight are for VERBATIM quotes or cited sources only, not paraphrasing

stylePreferences.colorScheme: warm muted tones — sepia accents, gold highlights on dark backgrounds
